clue.text: What changed hooter? The answer may be seen in hedges!

indicators.note: changed tells us the letters of the word what are to be put into a new order

parts.note: a hooter is a horn, as on an old motor car

explanation.surface: A puzzled query about an altered car horn, followed by a hint about hedgerows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changed' turns WHAT into HAWT; add HORN for the hooter. 'The answer' is a link pointing at the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: This thorny shrub, also called may, is the classic plant of English farm hedgerows.

clue.text: Lone miner was mad with Alice

explanation.surface: A solitary prospector who went crazy in the company of a girl called Alice.
explanation.walkthrough: In Australian slang a miner who works alone is a hatter; the Mad Hatter is a character Alice meets in Wonderland.
explanation.definitionFit: Australian slang names a solitary digger thus, and Lewis Carroll's tea-party host in Wonderland is famously mad.

clue.text: Gate used by cricketers

explanation.surface: A gateway that cricket players walk through.
explanation.walkthrough: The first sense is a small gate or door set into a larger one; the second is the stumps and bails in cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: A small side door or gate shares its name with the three stumps a bowler aims at in cricket.

clue.text: Empty talk but it gives a lift to aeronauts

definitions.text: it gives a lift to aeronauts

explanation.surface: Idle chatter compared with what keeps balloonists up.
explanation.definitionFit: Idle boasting is called this, and heated gas is what raises a balloon off the ground.

clue.text: Family hunt in meeting place

parts.note: a race is a family line or stock
to course is to hunt hares with hounds

explanation.surface: A family's hunt gathering at an agreed spot.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'meeting' is also a horse-racing fixture, so the meeting place is where the horses run.
explanation.definitionFit: A race meeting is a day of horse races, held at a track built for them.

clue.text: Indian doctor with a bird

parts.note: MO is Medical Officer, an army doctor
a hawk is a bird of prey

explanation.surface: A Native American physician accompanied by a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A people of the Iroquois confederacy, Native Americans of New York state and Canada.

clue.text: Trample upon and annul

explanation.surface: Crushing something underfoot and then cancelling it.
explanation.definitionFit: To ride roughshod over something tramples it; to set aside a decision or veto cancels it.

clue.text: A metal container, to this extent, contains a prickly plant

parts.note: a can is a tin, a metal container
thus means so far, to this degree

explanation.surface: A tin, so far as it goes, holds a spiny plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'contains' is a link word here, not a container signal: the three pieces sit side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: A Mediterranean herb with spiny leaves, whose foliage is carved on Corinthian capitals.

clue.text: Store Japanese liquor as a memento

parts.note: to keep something is to store it
sake is Japanese rice wine

explanation.surface: Putting away a bottle of Japanese rice wine as a souvenir.
explanation.definitionFit: A keepsake is a small object kept in remembrance of someone, a souvenir.

clue.text: Double credit for a child's watch

indicators.note: double says the word for credit is written two times over

parts.note: to buy on tick is to buy on credit

explanation.surface: Giving twice the credit for a youngster's wristwatch.
explanation.walkthrough: Buying 'on tick' is British for buying on credit.
explanation.definitionFit: Nursery speech for a clock or watch imitates the sound it makes.

clue.text: Iron man and woman

parts.note: Fe is the chemical symbol for iron
male means a man

explanation.surface: A list of iron, a man and a woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words denote a person of the sex that bears young, so either stands for the other.

clue.text: Observe man on board from end of telescope

parts.note: to eye something is to observe it
a chess or draughts man is a piece on the board

explanation.surface: Watching a chessman from the far end of a telescope.
explanation.walkthrough: 'man on board' suggests a sailor; it is a chess piece.
explanation.definitionFit: The lens one looks through sits at the viewer's end of a telescope or microscope.

clue.text: Kind of wig worn by Shakespearean character?

explanation.surface: A wig worn by an actor playing a figure from Shakespeare.
explanation.walkthrough: A brutus was an 18th-century short rough wig; the other sense is the conspirator in Julius Caesar.
explanation.definitionFit: A cropped Georgian hairpiece took its name from the Roman conspirator, who appears in Julius Caesar.

clue.text: A daintily pleasing point of view, but it's less than square

parts.note: cute means attractive in a dainty way
an angle is a viewpoint or slant

explanation.surface: A charming outlook that is nonetheless not quite conventional.
explanation.walkthrough: 'square' looks like 'old-fashioned'; it is a right angle of ninety degrees.
explanation.definitionFit: Any corner under ninety degrees, smaller than a right angle, is so called in geometry.

clue.text: Dazed and reeling from alcoholic beverage consumed

parts.note: punch is a mixed alcoholic drink
drunk is the past participle of drink, so consumed

explanation.surface: Someone groggy and staggering after a bowl of spirits.
explanation.definitionFit: Boxers stunned by repeated blows become confused and unsteady, so the word covers anyone groggy.

clue.text: Ship's company in halt could it be connected with a bottle-neck?

definitions.text: could it be connected with a bottle-neck

indicators.note: in tells us the crew sits inside the word for halt

parts.note: to stop is to halt
a ship's crew is its company

explanation.surface: A ship's crew stopped, wondering about a traffic bottleneck.
explanation.walkthrough: A bottleneck suggests a traffic jam; read it as the neck of a bottle, which a threaded cap fits.
explanation.definitionFit: A lid with a thread fastens onto a bottle's threaded neck by twisting.

clue.text: Nutty protein for a chap to eat

parts.note: a chap is a man
to dine is to eat a meal

explanation.surface: A nut-based protein bar offered as a meal for a man.
explanation.definitionFit: A protein found in almonds; also, a dish garnished with almonds.

clue.text: Not to mention refraining from interference

explanation.surface: Saying nothing about it and keeping one's hands off.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means 'much less' in argument, and also to leave something undisturbed.

clue.text: Counterbalance to make amends for

explanation.surface: Offsetting something in order to make up for it.
explanation.definitionFit: To offset one force with another, and to recompense someone for a loss or wrong.

clue.text: A soft fruit it would seem

parts.note: p is piano, the musical direction for soft
a pear is a fruit

explanation.surface: A ripe pear that only looks soft.
explanation.definitionFit: To look or seem a certain way is to give an impression of it.

clue.text: Shaped like an orange a dedicated person offered up

explanation.surface: An orange-shaped object held up by a devoted believer.
explanation.walkthrough: The first sense is flattened at the poles, like an orange or the Earth; the second is a layperson dedicated to a religious order.
explanation.definitionFit: Geometry calls a spheroid squashed at the poles this, and a lay member of a monastery bears the same name.

clue.text: Small body in space bumped into mixed ore

parts.note: to bump into someone is to meet them

indicators.note: mixed tells us the letters of ore are jumbled

explanation.surface: A small rock in orbit colliding with a jumble of ore.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bumped into' reads as a collision in the surface, but it means encountered someone.
explanation.definitionFit: A shooting star is a small rocky fragment burning up in the atmosphere.

clue.text: Number nine-may need an alteration

indicators.note: alteration says the letters of need and an are to be changed into a new order

explanation.surface: Ninth on the list might need some adjusting.
explanation.definitionFit: A group or set of nine, from the Greek for nine.

clue.text: Substantial material that can be felt

explanation.surface: Solid fabric you can touch.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means real and tangible, and literally able to be touched with the hands.

clue.text: One who cuts and stitches to join end to end with gold

parts.note: to tail things is to join them end to end
or is the heraldic word for gold

explanation.surface: A seamstress joining pieces end to end with gold thread.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who makes and alters clothes cuts cloth and sews it.

clue.text: Getting hot and cold confection could produce internal disorder

parts.note: ague is a fever with hot and cold fits
a cake is a sweet confection

explanation.surface: Feverish shivers after a dessert that might upset the stomach.
explanation.walkthrough: An old name for a swollen spleen caused by repeated malarial fever.
explanation.definitionFit: A hardened enlargement of the spleen, a bodily ailment following malaria.

clue.text: Old copper kitchen implement

explanation.surface: An antique copper utensil in a kitchen.
explanation.walkthrough: Peeler was early slang for a policeman, after Sir Robert Peel who founded the London police; 'copper' is not the metal.
explanation.definitionFit: Victorian police were nicknamed after their founder Robert Peel, and a tool strips skins off potatoes.

clue.text: Dusty-miller tolerates Spike

parts.note: bears means puts up with
an ear is the spike of a cereal plant holding the grain

explanation.surface: A dusty flour-miller puts up with a spike.
explanation.walkthrough: Dusty-miller is a folk name for the auricula, a primula whose leaves look floury.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are folk names for the auricula, an alpine primula.
